source.citation: MP, DB, RRSP, DPSP, ALDA, TFSA limits and the YMPE — RRSP dollar limit row, 2026

ca.federal.rrspDollarLimit2026.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. CRA limits table: 2026 $33,810 (2025 $32,490).

source.citation: RRSP contribution room — 18% of prior year earned income, less pension adjustment

ca.federal.rrspEarnedIncomeRate.note: NOT CONFIRMED. The CRA contribution-room page returned 404 on 2026-08-11, so the 18% rate was not read off a primary source. Room is 18% of prior-year EARNED income (a defined subset — employment, self-employment, rental; investment income does not qualify) OR the annual dollar limit, whichever is less, minus the pension adjustment. Find a live CRA page before signing off.

source.citation: TFSA contribution room — annual limit, 2026

ca.federal.tfsaAnnualLimit2026.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. CRA limits table: $7,000 for both 2026 and 2025. Indexed in $500 increments so it does not move every year. Withdrawals restore room on 1 January of the FOLLOWING year, not immediately.

source.citation: First Home Savings Account — annual participation room

ca.federal.fhsaAnnualLimit.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. $8,000 participation room in the first year and each year after. Unused room carries forward to a maximum of $8,000 into the following year — the carry-forward is capped, not unlimited.

source.citation: First Home Savings Account — lifetime contribution limit

ca.federal.fhsaLifetimeLimit.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. $40,000 lifetime maximum, across all FHSAs held.

source.citation: Home Buyers' Plan — maximum withdrawal amount

ca.federal.hbpWithdrawalLimit.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. CRA states 'Currently, the HBP withdrawal limit is $60,000.' Repayment schedule and the grace period before repayments begin are separate rules and are not yet captured here.

source.citation: Property transfer tax — general property transfer tax rate

ca.bc.pttSchedule.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. 1% up to and including $200,000; 2% above $200,000 up to and including $2,000,000; 3% above $2,000,000. See also the residential surcharge above $3,000,000.

source.citation: Property transfer tax — further 2% tax on residential property worth over $3,000,000

ca.bc.pttResidentialSurchargeAbove3m.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. Source: 'If the property has residential property worth over $3,000,000, a further 2% tax will be applied to the residential property value greater than $3,000,000.' Mixed-class property: applies to the residential portion only. This band was ABSENT from the project docs.

source.citation: Property transfer tax — residential value threshold for the further 2% tax
First Time Home Buyers' Program — partial exemption upper bound

ca.bc.pttFtbPhaseOutCeiling.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. Partial exemption applies where fair market value is more than $835,000 but less than $860,000; the exemption is eliminated at $860,000.

source.citation: Newly Built Home Exemption — full exemption threshold

ca.bc.pttNewBuildFullExemptionCeiling.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. 'Effective April 1, 2024, the fair market value threshold for a full exemption for newly built homes is increased from $750,000 to $1,100,000.' Unlike the first-time buyers' program, the source describes no cap on the exemption amount at a lower value.

source.citation: Newly Built Home Exemption — partial exemption upper bound

ca.bc.pttNewBuildPhaseOutCeiling.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. Phase-out range is $50,000 above the threshold, eliminated completely at $1,150,000.

source.citation: Mortgage loan insurance cost — premium rate by loan-to-value ratio

ca.mortgage.cmhcPremiumBands.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and CORRECTED. Published table, premium on total loan by loan-to-value: up to 65% 0.60%; 65.01-75% 1.70%; 75.01-80% 2.40%; 80.01-85% 2.80%; 85.01-90% 3.10%; 90.01-95% 4.00%; 90.01-95% with a non-traditional down payment 4.50%. Project docs held only three bands expressed as down payment. Premiums in Quebec, Ontario and Saskatchewan attract provincial sales tax — not modelled.

source.citation: Mortgage loan insurance — when mortgage loan insurance is required

ca.mortgage.cmhcInsuranceRequiredBelowDo.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. CMHC eligibility states insurance applies where the down payment is less than 20%; at or above 20% it is not required.

source.citation: Mortgage loan insurance — maximum purchase price eligibility

ca.mortgage.cmhcMaxInsurablePrice.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and CORRECTED from $1,000,000 to $1,500,000. CMHC eligibility: purchase price / lending value must be below $1,500,000 for homeowner loans. Homes above $1.5M are not eligible and require 20% down. The $1,000,000 in the project docs was stale by a policy change and would have denied eligibility to a whole band of purchases.

source.citation: Minimum down payment requirements

ca.mortgage.minDownPaymentRateLowerBand.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. 5% minimum for a purchase price of $500,000 or less; above that, 5% on the first $500,000 and 10% on the remainder.

source.citation: Minimum down payment requirements — band threshold
Minimum down payment requirements — rate above the band threshold

ca.mortgage.minDownPaymentRateUpperBand.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. 10% on the portion above $500,000.

source.citation: First Time Home Buyers' Program — current exemption amounts, full exemption threshold

ca.bc.pttFtbEligibilityCeiling.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and RENAMED — the previous name was wrong, not just the framing. $835,000 is the fair-market-value CEILING for eligibility, effective 1 April 2024. It is NOT the value up to which tax is fully exempt: the exemption AMOUNT is capped at the tax on the first $500,000. See ca.bc.pttFtbExemptionCapValue. Modelling $835,000 as a full exemption overstates the benefit on any home above $500,000.

source.citation: First Time Home Buyers' Programme — exemption applies to the first $500,000 of purchase price

ca.bc.pttFtbExemptionCapValue.note: Primary source read 2026-08-11 and confirmed. NEW — this constant did not exist and its absence was a defect. The exemption equals the tax payable on the first $500,000, not the full tax. On an $800,000 home the buyer still pays tax on $300,000. Source: 'the purchaser will be exempt from property transfer tax on the first $500,000 of the purchase price.'
